core_obligations: For (1), replace a representing complex M^bullet by tau_{<=0}M^bullet so that M^i = 0 for i > 0 (proof lines 22317-22319).
Choose a free resolution P^bullet -> M^bullet with P^i = 0 for i > 0, quoting the existence of suitable left resolutions in the derived category (proof lines 22319-22321).
Set K^bullet = tau_{>=-1}P^bullet to obtain the required two-term complex with K^0 free (proof line 22322).
For (2), use the pseudo-coherence statement to choose a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet -> M^bullet with F^i = 0 for i > 0 and F^i finite free (proof lines 22325-22327).
Set K^bullet = tau_{>=-1}F^bullet, so that K^0 is finite free and K^{-1} is finite (proof line 22328).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and an object K of D(R) whose cohomology vanishes outside degrees -1 and 0, and asserts two things: K can be represented by a two-term complex K^{-1} -> K^0 with K^0 free, and if R is Noetherian with H^{-1}(K) and H^0(K) finite, then K can be represented by such a complex with K^0 finite free and K^{-1} finite (source lines 22303-22314). Both halves are constructive. For (1), the proof replaces a representing complex of modules M^bullet by its truncation tau_{<=0}M^bullet, so that M^i vanishes for i > 0; chooses a free resolution P^bullet -> M^bullet with P^i = 0 for i > 0, quoting the existence of left resolutions in the derived category; and sets K^bullet = tau_{>=-1}P^bullet (proof lines 22317-22322). For (2), it uses the pseudo-coherence statement to choose a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet -> M^bullet with F^i = 0 for i > 0 and all F^i finite free, and again truncates, setting K^bullet = tau_{>=-1}F^bullet (proof lines 22325-22328). The non-routine content is the choice of truncation window: truncating above degree 0 and below degree -1 leaves exactly a two-term complex, and the freeness of K^0 is read off from the resolution, while in the Noetherian finite case the finiteness of K^{-1} comes from the finite free resolution.
